Job Type:

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Provide front line leadership, support, mentoring and service in all geology activities, associated with exploration and resource drilling, core processing, sample analysis and resource evaluation.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Manage all Exploration sampling activities – including but not limited to drilling, rock chip, soil sampling.
Surveying and mapping designated areas / prospects.
Analysing geological data using specialist computer applications.
Preparing reports, both internal and statutory, physicals and forecast. Complete all reports in a timely manner, adhering to strict deadlines.
Ensure correct QA/QC protocols are adhered to.
Drill hole planning, designs and roll out.
About You
To be considered for this position, candidates must have bachelor’s Degree in Geology, Geophysics, or Geoscience with a minimum of 7 years’ experience in exploration work. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite and the ability to analyse numerical and graphical data, including experience with 3D modelling software.
Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble-shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

27399.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
The Superintendent H&S – Underground is responsible for providing visible safety leadership and strategic H&S support to K92's Underground Operations.
The role partners with Underground operational leaders to identify, assess and control critical risks, strengthen operational discipline, improve workforce capability and ensure compliance with company standards and regulatory requirements.
The Superintendent H&S – Underground will spend significant time in the field engaging with leaders and work crews, verifying critical controls, coaching supervisors and supporting a proactive safety culture focused on learning, risk ownership and continuous improvement.
The role is accountable for ensuring that underground health and safety systems are effectively implemented and that underground operations are conducted in a manner that protects people, the environment, equipment and the business.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Provide visible and credible safety leadership across Underground Operations.
Develop strong working relationships with operational leaders, supervisors and work crews.
Promote a culture of personal accountability, risk ownership and continuous improvement.
Coach frontline leaders in effective field leadership, risk management and safety engagement practices.
Build leadership capability through coaching, mentoring and field-based learning.
Support the development of a positive reporting and learning culture.
Support the implementation and verification of fatal risk management and critical control programs.
Maintain oversight of underground risk registers, TARPs and critical risk management plans.
Facilitate risk assessments for high risk and non-routine work activities.
Monitor emerging risks and ensure effective controls are implemented and maintained.
Maintain a strong visible field presence underground.
Conduct workplace inspections, leadership interactions and task observations.
Verify compliance with site standards, procedures and critical control requirements.
Identify opportunities to improve operational discipline and workforce behaviours.
Lead investigations into significant and high potential incidents.
Verify corrective actions are practical, effective and sustainable.
Share lessons learned across the organisation.
Support the implementation and continual improvement of H&S management systems including SkyTrust.
Support the development, implementation and verification of H&S standards, critical control standards and safe work practices.
Participate in internal assurance activities and management system audits.
Monitor performance indicators and identify trends requiring intervention.
Support the development of underground safety leadership capability.
Assist with development and delivery of H&S training programs.
Mentor supervisors, safety representatives and emerging safety professionals.
Support underground emergency response preparedness.
Participate in emergency planning, exercises and reviews.
Assist with development of underground emergency procedures and response capability.
Ensure compliance with applicable PNG legislation, MRA requirements and company standards.
Support regulatory inspections and audits.
Prepare reports and documentation required by regulators and company management.
About You
To be considered for this role, you must have a tertiary qualification in relevant field with a minimum of 4 years’ experience as Safety Superintendent in Mining, Oil or Gas Industry. In addition to this, you will have most or all of the following.
Diploma or Degree in Occupational Health and Safety, Mining Engineering, or related discipline.
Minimum 5 years' experience in a senior H&S role within mining, including experience supporting underground operations.
Demonstrated experience leading incident investigations.
Training in ICAM or equivalent investigation methodology.
Training in auditing and assurance processes.
Underground metalliferous mining experience.
Current PNG Driver's Licence.
Emergency response experience.
Training and assessment qualifications.
Exposure to critical control management systems.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

Location:

Position Overview
The Salesperson is responsible for assisting walk‑in customers, processing sales orders, and ensuring excellent service at the counter. This role focuses on selling HVAC equipment, spare parts, and related accessories while supporting smooth counter operations and contributing to overall sales performance.
Key Responsibilities
Customer Service & Sales
Greet and assist walk‑in customers, technicians, and contractors at the counter.
Recommend appropriate products, spare parts, tools, and solutions based on customer needs.
Prepare and issue quotes, process sales invoices, and handle EFTPOS transactions.
Product Knowledge & Technical Support
Learn and stay updated on new product lines, specifications, and promotions.
Inventory & Stock Handling
Coordinate with warehouse staff to ensure timely picking and delivery of counter orders.
Check stock availability and provide accurate information to customers.
Assist with stock checks, labelling, shelving, and maintaining a tidy counter area.
Documentation & Record Keeping
Process all sales documents accurately (dockets, receipts, quotations).
Maintain customer files and ensure correct pricing and product codes.
Follow company policies for returns, warranty claims, and special orders.
Teamwork & Communication
Work closely with warehouse staff, procurement, and management.
Communicate customer feedback, product issues, or supply concerns to supervisors.
Support overall branch sales goals and daily counter operations.
Health, Safety & Compliance
Follow all workplace health and safety guidelines.
Ensure safe handling of HVAC parts and materials, including refrigerants and electrical components.
Maintain a clean, safe, and professional counter environment.
Skills & Competencies
Strong customer service and communication skills.
Basic understanding of HVAC systems or mechanical/electrical products (preferred).
Ability to read product codes, specs, and part numbers.
Good computer skills (POS systems, email, basic Excel).
Sales-driven mindset with attention to accuracy and detail.
Qualifications & Experience
Grade 12 certificate preferred.
Experience in retail, trade counter sales, or technical sales an advantage.
Prior exposure to HVAC, mechanical, plumbing, or electrical products highly beneficial.
Experience in fast-paced customer service or parts counter work preferred.
Personal Attributes
Friendly, approachable, and customer focused.
Reliable, organised, and proactive.
Willingness to learn technical products.
Team player with a positive attitude.

27891.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
As the Supervisor – Transport & Logistics, you will play a critical role in keeping Newmont’s Lihir operation moving safely, efficiently, and reliably. Leading a diverse team of transport professionals, you will oversee the movement of people, materials, and equipment across site operations, ensuring transportation services are delivered to the highest standards of safety, performance, and operational excellence. Your leadership will directly influence productivity, fleet efficiency, and the safe execution of logistics activities across the business.
As part of our team, you will
Lead and supervise a transport and logistics workforce, including drivers and mobile equipment operators.
Coordinate daily transportation schedules for personnel, materials, and equipment to support operational requirements.
Monitor fleet availability, vehicle utilisation, and fuel consumption to maximise operational efficiency.
Ensure compliance with safety standards, load restraint requirements, and chain of responsibility obligations across all transport activities.
Supervise loading and unloading activities to protect people, equipment, and materials.
Manage transport records, databases, manifests, and operational documentation with accuracy and attention to detail.
Support the resolution of transport disruptions, equipment breakdowns, and logistics challenges while maintaining service continuity.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance transport efficiency, productivity, and service delivery.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive, you will bring:
Proven experience in transport and logistics operations, ideally with 5+ years in a similar environment.
Demonstrated leadership experience managing teams in operational or industrial settings.
Strong understanding of transport regulations, load restraint practices, and chain of responsibility requirements.
A genuine commitment to safety leadership and safe work practices.
Strong planning, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
Excellent communication skills with the ability to build productive relationships across diverse teams and stakeholders.
Sound computer literacy, including Microsoft Office and the ability to work within business systems and transport management processes.
Experience working within large, complex organisations, preferably in mining, heavy industry, logistics, or related sectors.
Your work environment
Located in Lihir, Papua New Guinea, you will join Newmont's Supply Chain team and report to the Superintendent – Ports, Warehouse & Logistics. You will lead a team responsible for transportation services across a dynamic and fast-paced mining operation, working closely with operational stakeholders to deliver safe and efficient logistics outcomes. This is an opportunity to build your leadership capability through ongoing mentoring and coaching while contributing to a world-class mining business recognised for its strong safety culture, operational excellence, and commitment to its people.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​
Learn more about our purpose and values:
About Newmont
​
Hear from our people:
Life at Newmont
​
Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team:
[email protected]
.
Apply

27808.description:
Simberi Gold Company Limited’s operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking an
Operational Readiness – Reliability Engineer
to join our team, on a Fixed-Term (Two-Year) contract to fill a position for our Simberi Operation. This position will be based in Port Moresby and will be working Monday to Friday.  Site travel will be required occasionally.
Reporting to the Manager – Planning & Reliability, this role will provide technical reliability expertise in relation to master data development in Pronto for all new assets installed as part of the New Simberi Gold Project. The purpose is to ensure that master data is developed based on reliability centred principals and in compliance with Pronto standards in order for the expanded plant to safely achieve high equipment availability and asset utilisation in a manner consistent with the Company’s Vision and Values.
The opportunity
Technical accountabilities
Ensure safe work practices by identifying hazards, reporting risks, and adhering to health and safety standards to protect self and others when visiting site.
Reliability support on the master data development for the New Simberi Gold Project.
Provide weekly updates to OR – Planning & Reliability Specialist.

This role is to ensure that WV Papua New Guinea actively collaborates with Partners and Donors to ensure:

Grant Funding contract Compliance and expected accountabilities are exceeded.

27806.description:
Operational Readiness – Mechanical Engineer
Simberi Gold Company Limited’s operations consist of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking an
Operational Readiness – Mechanical Engineer
to join our team, on a Fixed-Term (Two-Year) contract to fill a position for our Simberi Operation. This position will be based in Port Moresby and will be working Monday to Friday.  Site travel will be required occasionally.
Reporting to the Manager – Planning & Reliability, this role will provide technical reliability expertise in relation to master data development in Pronto for all new assets installed as part of the New Simberi Gold Project. The purpose is to ensure that master data is developed based on reliability centred principals and in compliance with Pronto standards in order for the expanded plant to safely achieve high equipment availability and asset utilisation in a manner consistent with the Company’s Vision and Values
The opportunity
Technical accountabilities
Ensure safe work practices by identifying hazards, reporting risks, and adhering to health and safety standards to protect self and others when visiting site.
Mechanical Engineering and master data development for the New Simberi Gold Project.
Provide weekly updates to OR – Planning & Reliability Specialist.
Review of all current plant failure modes and provide input to the Asset Management Plans for all new equipment listed in Mechanical, Electrical and Instrument equipment lists.
Support Reliability Engineers with techniques and tools (RCM, FMEA) to optimise Asset Management Plans. Participate as team member in development of asset failure mode analysis.
Assist with the development of master data upload sheets specifically in relation to full spare parts catalogues, ANSIs for recommended spare parts and spares bill of materials for PM tasks.
Ensure all existing failure modes are accurately translated into Asset Strategies.
Review condition-monitoring strategies and establish (vibration, oil, thermography, NDT) to inform maintenance planning, condition-based maintenance, and replacement decisions.
Collaborate with operations, maintenance, engineering to ensure all improvement opportunities are embedded in future PMs.
Ensure compliance with safety, environmental, and regulatory requirements in all Asset Management Plans.
Make recommendations for the removal of redundant equipment and spare parts from Pronto as required.
Contribute to building operational readiness team capabilities, ensuring work meets requirements, and support professional development initiatives.
Engage with cross-functional teams and contractors, fostering collaboration, communication, and compliance with safety and environmental regulations.
Follow project governance frameworks (e.g., Simberi Project Charter) including business case development, scope definition, risk assessment, stakeholder engagement, and reporting.
Scheduling accountabilities
Managing effective use of available resources, including own time, in support of the delivery of the team/crew.
People accountabilities
Sharing knowledge and contributing to the development of capability within the operational readiness team.
Contributing to an effective team in a remote working environment.
Ensuring own work performance meets all role requirements; and taking appropriate professional development actions.
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara’s Values
Efficient MS Word, MS Excel
Bachelor of Engineering in related engineering field
At least 5 years relevant site experience with sound knowledge of RCM principles
Strong ability to work effectively within a team and work to tight deadlines
Strong communication skills, including communicating with people from different backgrounds and cultures
Demonstrated flexibility and ability to manage multiple priorities in a day.
Desirable
Asset Strategy and PM development on a greenfields or brownfields site.
Strong skills in computerized maintenance management systems, maintenance planning best practices, and relevant technical knowledge. Pronto experience highly regarded.
Familiarity with risk management and quality assurance principles.

Simberi Operations

27661.description:
About Newmont
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation is located on Aniolam Island in Papua New Guinea’s New Ireland Province. Lihir is one of the world’s largest producing gold operations and is situated within a geothermally active, extinct volcanic crater near the town of Londolovit. As a major open-pit gold operation, Lihir plays an important role in Newmont’s global portfolio and contributes significant economic and social value to Papua New Guinea and local communities.
Your role
As the Planner Shutdown, you will coordinate shutdown planning activities to support efficient scheduling, resource allocation and safe execution across the Lihir operation.
This role will see you prepare detailed shutdown plans, develop work packages, coordinate resources and work closely with maintenance and operations teams to align shutdown activity. You will play an important role in supporting safe, well-planned shutdown execution through practical planning, effective communication, risk management and continuous monitoring of shutdown progress.
Key Responsibilities
Prepare detailed shutdown plans and schedules to support safe and efficient execution.
Collaborate with maintenance and operations teams to align shutdown activities with operational requirements.
Prepare and provide shutdown work packages, documentation and supporting information.
Monitor shutdown progress and adjust schedules as required to support delivery.
Assess and obtain the necessary materials, resources and information required for shutdown activities.
Administer risk assessments and implement mitigation strategies to support safe execution.
Monitor and report on shutdown performance metrics, identifying opportunities for improvement.
Support compliance with safety and environmental regulations throughout shutdown activities.
Administer pre-shutdown meetings, including shutdown charter reviews and approvals, to align all team members.
Assess relevant risks, implement mitigation measures and continuously monitor risk throughout shutdown planning and execution.
Your Skills & Experience
Trade qualification or relevant experience in maintenance, shutdowns, operations or asset management.
Significant applied experience as a maintenance tradesperson or in a maintenance-related role.
Experience in shutdown planning, coordination and scheduling.
Knowledge of statutory regulations and safety requirements relevant to shutdown activities.
Knowledge of multiple trades and shutdown interactions.
Proficiency in Microsoft Project, resource levelling and cost control techniques.
Experience conducting risk assessments to support safe shutdown execution.
Experience scoping tasks to enable safe and effective work delivery.
Project management skills, with the ability to coordinate work packages, schedules and resources.
Strong communication and collaboration skills, with the ability to build positive working relationships across maintenance, operations and support teams.
Desirable experience includes frontline leadership or supervision experience, advanced proficiency in shutdown planning and coordination, extensive knowledge of risk management and safety compliance, and experience working in mining, processing, heavy industry or site-based maintenance environments.
Work Environment & Benefits
This is a full-time FIFO role based at Lihir Gold Limited in Papua New Guinea, working on a 3 weeks on / 3 weeks off roster. You will support Operations and Asset Management. You will work closely with maintenance, operations and shutdown teams to ensure planning activities are aligned, resourced and ready for safe execution.
You will be part of a team focused on effective shutdown preparation, practical work packaging, safe execution planning and continuous improvement across shutdown performance.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our people are our strength, and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.
Learn more about our purpose and values:
About Newmont

You will play a key role in ensuring accurate record keeping, efficient coordination of meetings and events, smooth calendar and schedule management, and the preparation of reports, presentations and other business documents. This role is suited to an organised, proactive and collaborative leader who can support team performance, maintain confidentiality and help deliver high-quality administrative services across the business.

Manage calendars and schedules to support effective time management for leaders and teams.
Coordinate office records and files, ensuring confidentiality, security and accurate record keeping.

Administer office expenses and budgets, including travel expense monitoring, budget tracking and expense reconciliation.
Support the team with purchase requisitions and payment requests through the invoicing system.

Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
BRIDGE-SA, Project Officer
CARE International in PNG is seeking a qualified and experienced Project Officer to support Building Replicable Implementation Dialogue and Governance through Social Accountability Project, Lae based. CARE is an international development and humanitarian aid organisation fighting global poverty, with a special focus on working with women and girls to bring lasting change to their communities. As a non-religious and non-political organisation, CARE works with communities to help overcome poverty by supporting development efforts and providing emergency assistance. We believe supporting women and girls is one of the most effective ways to create sustainable outcomes in poor communities.
The Project Officer BRIDGE-SA will support day-to-day implementation of the BRIDGE-SA project at community, facility, school and district levels. The role will assist with organising activities, engaging stakeholders, facilitating participation, documenting progress and supporting follow – up of agreed actions. This includes closely with communities, government counterparts, church agencies, civil society organisations, schools and health facilities to support delivery of social accountability activities across the health and education sectors in Morobe Province.
The project officer will play an important role in ensuring that project approaches are practical, inclusive, well – coordinated and responsive to local context.
The role requires strong relationship – building skills, attention to detail, and ability to work closely with communities and local stakeholders in respectful and accountable way.
The Project Officer will contribute to effective field implementation, stakeholder engagement, activity follow-up, documentation and reporting, while helping ensure that project activities are delivered in line with CARE’s commitments to
gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI), safeguarding, accountability, do no harm.
This position is based in Goroka and will require travel to field sites in Eastern Highlands Province and Morobe Province as required.
Key Responsibilities
Support implementation of project activities in line with approved workplans, schedules and budgets
Assist with organising field visits, meetings, workshops, trainings and community engagement activities
Support follow – up of project activities and agreed action points at community, school, facility and district levels.
Maintain accurate activity records, attendance lists, meeting notes and implementation files.
Develop quarterly work plans that are aligned to the annual project work plans and budget in order to meet the project activity deadlines.
Ensure that the work plans are consistent with envisaged outputs and objectives in the monitoring and evaluation framework
Participate in community awareness and socialisation activities
Contribute to and support project approaches that consider gender, protection, and inclusion issues;
Selection Criteria
Diploma or Degree in public health, education, development studies, governance, social sciences, project management or a related field;
At least 2 - 3 years relevant experience in coordinating or implementing development programs, preferably in health, education, governance or social accountability.
Experience supporting community engagement, training, facilitation or field based project activities
Working knowledge of Community Scorecard tools and processes
Good communication and relationship building skills
Understanding of GEDSI, safeguarding and inclusive programming
Ability to maintain clear documentation and support reporting requirements
Demonstrated organisational and time management skills, working in a team and the ability to work under pressure and to organise and manage workload and meet deadlines;
Basic competence in Microsoft Office Application
Desirable Experience
Experience working in Morobe and/or Eastern Highlands provinces
Familiarity with social accountability approaches, including scorecards, feedback systems, dialogue forums or governance strengthening
Experience in health and/or education sector programming
Experience working with donor-funded projects or NGO compliance systems
Experience working in partnership with church agencies or local civil society organisations

27882.description:
Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Project Officer – BRIDGE-SA Project
CARE International in PNG is seeking a qualified and experienced Project Officer to support Building Replicable Implementation Dialogue and Governance through Social Accountability Project, Goroka base. CARE is an international development and humanitarian aid organisation fighting global poverty, with a special focus on working with women and girls to bring lasting change to their communities. As a non-religious and non-political organisation, CARE works with communities to help overcome poverty by supporting development efforts and providing emergency assistance. We believe supporting women and girls is one of the most effective ways to create sustainable outcomes in poor communities.
The Project Officer BRIDGE-SA will support day-to-day implementation of the BRIDGE-SA project at community, facility, school and district levels. The role will assist with organising activities, engaging stakeholders, facilitating participation, documenting progress and supporting follow – up of agreed actions. This includes closely with communities, government counterparts, church agencies, civil society organisations, schools and health facilities to support delivery of social accountability activities across the health and education sectors in Eastern Highlands Province.
The project officer will play an important role in ensuring that project approaches are practical, inclusive, well – coordinated and responsive to local context.
The role requires strong relationship – building skills, attention to detail, and ability to work closely with communities and local stakeholders in respectful and accountable way.
The Project Officer will contribute to effective field implementation, stakeholder engagement, activity follow-up, documentation and reporting, while helping ensure that project activities are delivered in line with CARE’s commitments to
gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI), safeguarding, accountability, do no harm.
This position is based in Goroka and will require travel to field sites in Eastern Highlands Province and Morobe Province as required.

Support implementation of project activities in line with approved workplans, schedules and budgets

27864.description:
About this Role
The Geologist is responsible for the day to day execution of the exploration program, including planning on a short interval time horizon, liaison with drilling business partners and local contract employees and the accurate collection of many forms of data in line with procedure. Independent operation of the Geologists provides the Supervisor Exploration Geologist time to consolidate and interpret data more effectively and create new longer term plans accordingly.
Your role will consist of:
-- Create daily and weekly plans for drilling and associated earthworks activities or remote field operations that can be shared with internal and external stakeholders to enable their facilitation.
-- Complete detailed drill hole designs that provide drilling contractors and the exploration team the information required to execute the hole safely and efficiently.
-- Design remote field surface sampling programs that satisfy objectives provided by the Supervisor Exploration Geologist.
-- Collect and verify quality geological and geotechnical data from the logging of diamond or RC drill holes in line with procedure.
-- Lead remote field sampling activities involving teams of local contract employees ensuring safe execution and data quality.
-- Liaise with drilling contractors to acquire, analyse and verify drill hole surveys and advise on progress relative to plan and any remedial actions required.
-- Analyse data collected from drilling or sampling programs and recommend alterations to the forward exploration program, if necessary or appropriate.
-- Use technical knowledge of deposit classes together with exploratory data analysis and geological maps and models to develop exploration targets in near-mine and brownfields settings.
-- Rate and rank exploration targets to build a holistic prioritized exploration portfolio that will support budget applications.
-- Ensure that all Exploration activities are conducted in adherence with Newmont Always Safe and Fatality Risk Management protocols.
-- Participate in the Newmont Always Safe program by completing Critical Control Verifications and Field Interactions.
-- Foster a work environment in which team members feel comfortable speaking up on core topics like safety in the workplace and Respect At Work.
Your training, skills and experience checklist
Here is what we would need so see from you!
Required Knowledge & Experience (essential and desirable)
-- BSc (Hons) or higher degree in Geological / Geosciences.
-- Minimum 3 years industry experience, ideally within different geologic environments.
-- Native Microsoft Office skills are essential.
-- Experience using database software such as acQuire is essential.
-- Experience using mapping and modelling software (e.g., Leapfrog, ArcGIS) is essential.
-- A Class 6 PNG Drivers License is essential.
-- Fluency in both English and Tok Pisin is essential.
-- Effective written and verbal communication skills are essential.
-- Demonstrated planning and analytical skills are highly desirable.
-- Demonstrated ability to work independently is highly desirable.
-- A demonstrated focus on continuous improvement is highly desirable.
-- Ability to present technical information clearly and concisely to non-technical stakeholders is highly desirable.
Working conditions and location
The position is conducted on a 21/21 fly-in fly-out (FIFO) roster from approved ports of hire with additional work time as required to meet the requirements of the role. Working days are nominally 12 hours excluding travelling time between camp and the Lihir operation.
Our FIFO employees stay in secure and comfortable camp in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and annual incentive program.
We understand no candidate will meet every single desired qualification. If your experience looks a little different from what we’ve identified and you think you can bring value to the role, we’d love to learn more about you!
Newmont is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Underpinned by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility and Inclusion. Our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free of discrimination, as well as the cultures, religions, and governing codes applicable to each country in which we operate.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date 5th AUG 2026 – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

27863.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor Electrical, you will play a critical role in keeping essential power and electrical infrastructure operating safely, reliably, and efficiently. Working across power generation equipment, high-voltage and low-voltage distribution networks, transformers, switchgear, protection systems, and industrial infrastructure, you will help drive asset reliability, operational performance, and continuous improvement across a complex mining operation. Your expertise will directly support safe production outcomes while contributing to the development of people, systems, and electrical maintenance excellence.
As part of our team, you will
Lead and support safe electrical maintenance activities, ensuring compliance with site safety standards and electrical regulations.
Coordinate planned, corrective, and shutdown maintenance activities to maximize equipment availability and reliability.
Troubleshoot electrical faults and identify opportunities to improve equipment performance and asset health.
Monitor and maintain critical electrical assets including generators, transformers, switchgear, protection systems, MCCs, and distribution networks.
Work closely with maintenance teams, contractors, and operational stakeholders to deliver safe and reliable outcomes.
Manage maintenance records, work orders, and asset information using systems such as SAP Fusion Maintenance Management.
Support reliability improvement initiatives, condition monitoring programs, and continuous improvement projects that enhance operational performance.
Contribute to the growth and capability development of team members while building your own leadership and technical expertise
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this role, you will bring:
A current Electrical Trade Qualification / Licensed Electrician.
Demonstrated experience in electrical maintenance, operations, or asset management within mining, power generation, utilities, or heavy industrial environments.
Strong knowledge of HV and LV electrical distribution systems, generators, transformers, switchgear, protection systems, and power infrastructure.
Experience coordinating tradespeople, contractors, and maintenance activities in a safety-critical environment.
A proactive, safety-first mindset with the ability to conduct risk assessments, manage permit-to-work processes, and promote safe work practices.
Strong planning, communication, collaboration, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work effectively across diverse teams.
Experience using maintenance management systems such as SAP Fusion, SAP PM, or similar platforms.
Certifications such as HV Switching Authorisation, LOTO/PTW training, and electrical safety qualifications will be highly regarded.
Your work environment
You'll join a collaborative team that values safety, technical excellence, continuous improvement, and professional growth. This role works closely with the Electrical Superintendent, maintenance personnel, and contractors to support critical power and utilities infrastructure. You'll enjoy a dynamic environment where no two days are the same, balancing hands-on field engagement with maintenance coordination, reliability improvement, and strategic asset performance initiatives.
This position offers genuine career development opportunities, with pathways into broader electrical leadership, asset management, and superintendent-level roles. You'll also gain exposure to emerging technologies, predictive maintenance tools, SAP analytics, and condition monitoring systems that will strengthen your technical and leadership capabilities.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 (day shift only) Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why join Newmont
Work in a remote operational environment supporting critical electrical and power infrastructure.
Engage with a diverse range of stakeholders including maintenance teams, contractors, and operational leaders.
Be part of an inclusive workplace that encourages applications from women, local nationals, and underrepresented groups while championing diversity, equity, and inclusion.
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 43383 before the advertised closing date: 5 August 2026.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Apply

27652.description:
Drive operational excellence, partner performance, and customer experience.
Lead retail performance for a leading energy and retail organisation.
Support revenue growth through retail opportunities in a competitive market.
The Opportunity
Our client, a leading organisation in the energy and retail sector, is seeking a strategic and results-driven Retail Executive to oversee retail network performance across the Southern Region. This role focuses on driving operational excellence, optimising retail partner performance, enhancing the customer experience, and expanding complementary revenue streams in a highly competitive market.
The Role
In this role, you will manage a portfolio of retail sites to ensure operational and commercial excellence. You will drive compliance with HSEQ standards, optimise sales performance, and implement effective marketing and customer service strategies. As a key commercial driver, you will manage commercial agreements, oversee credit control, analyse market activity, and identify opportunities to maximise revenue across the retail network.
Key Responsibilities
Oversee retail network performance across the region, managing a portfolio of retail sites and driving sales performance across multiple product and service categories.
Promote a strong safety culture across the retail network, ensuring retail partners, staff and contractors comply with HSEQ policies, procedures and standards.
Manage the commercial aspects of retail partner agreements, including analysing forecast and actual profit and loss performance, monitoring monthly sales against targets, and managing credit and payment terms.
Develop and implement local marketing initiatives to increase customer traffic, train retail partners on operational standards, and foster a customer-focused service culture to achieve annual targets.
Identify and negotiate opportunities to maximise revenue through complementary retail services and strategic partnerships.
Conduct market analysis to monitor competitor activity, support commercial business growth, and participate in retail partner recruitment initiatives.
Monitor inventory and operational performance, manage environmental risks, and ensure contractual compliance across the retail network.
Qualifications and Experience
Bachelor's degree in business, marketing, commerce or a related discipline.
3–5 years' experience in account management, preferably within the retail, oil and gas, or FMCG sectors.
Strong technical skills in account management, credit control, contract compliance, and financial analysis, including profit and loss reporting and sales performance reporting.
Demonstrated experience in sales and marketing initiatives, customer service monitoring, and retail partner training.
Familiarity with HSEQ compliance. Knowledge of HACCP or food hygiene standards will be highly regarded.
Excellent communication, presentation, negotiation and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to influence a diverse range of internal and external stakeholders.
Professional working proficiency in written and spoken English. Knowledge of Tok Pisin will be an advantage.
If you are a results-driven professional with strong financial analysis and negotiation skills, ready to drive operational excellence across our client's retail network, please register your interest by clicking
'APPLY NOW'
and submitting your most recent CV in Microsoft Word format.

27387.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is responsible for carrying out electrical breakdown and preventative maintenance repairs on a wide range of mobile equipment’s including Light Vehicles, Boggers, Truck fleet, Excavators, Drills, Dozers, Graders, and support equipment.
Key Accountabilities
Performing scheduled and Breakdown maintenance on a large fleet of Underground Mining Equipment including Sandvik Drills, Trucks and Loaders with an ancillary fleet of CAT and Normet equipment.
Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment’s and machines.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment’s, and machines.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a NATTB certified Trade certificate in Auto-electrical with at least 3-5 years of relevant work experience in heavy industry preferably mining environment. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Demonstrated experience in maintaining electrical equipment in the mobile fleet including Drills, Trucks, Loaders as well as Light vehicles, Dozers, excavators, graders,
Relevant experience in automotive air conditioning systems.
Self-motivated with ability to always work autonomously.
Strong safety focus and sound knowledge of standard operating procedures.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
As Advisor, Security, you will play a critical role in protecting people, assets, and operations at one of the world's leading mining companies. Reporting to the Team Lead - Security, you will oversee daily site security operations, lead frontline security personnel, and help create a safe and secure environment for employees, contractors, and visitors. Your work will directly contribute to operational continuity, incident prevention, emergency response, and the ongoing improvement of security systems and processes across site operations.
As part of our team, you will
Lead and support daily site security operations, ensuring compliance with established security procedures and standards.
Supervise and coordinate a team of Newmont Security Officers and contracted security personnel.
Conduct security inspections, patrols, surveys, and risk assessments to identify and address potential threats.
Investigate security incidents, prepare detailed reports, and support joint investigations with relevant stakeholders and authorities where required.
Review and maintain security documentation, standard operating procedures, and officer reports to ensure accuracy and compliance.
Coordinate emergency response activities and deploy security resources effectively during critical incidents.
Mentor, coach, and develop security personnel through training, guidance, and performance support.
Build strong working relationships across site teams, camp management, contractors, and external agencies.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this position, you will bring:
•    A minimum of 5 years' experience in security, law enforcement, military, or a related field, preferably within the resources or mining sector.
•    Experience leading security teams and coordinating security operations in a complex environment.
•    Proven experience conducting investigations, security surveys, risk assessments, and incident reporting.
•    Strong computer literacy with the ability to prepare reports, maintain records, and manage documentation effectively.
•    Knowledge of physical security practices, emergency response procedures, and relevant compliance requirements.
•    A valid Class 6 driver's license.
•    The ability to obtain and maintain a Police Clearance and Security Industry Authority (SIA) certification or equivalent requirements.
•    Personal qualities that include integrity, accountability, trustworthiness, sound judgement, and a collaborative leadership style.
Your work environment
Located at our Lihir operation, this role offers the opportunity to work within a close-knit and highly respected security team that plays a vital role in supporting safe, responsible mining operations. You'll collaborate with a diverse workforce, engage with internal and external stakeholders, and have the opportunity to influence security standards and continuous improvement initiatives. The team has a strong track record of developing talent from within, creating genuine pathways for career progression and leadership growth.
We are committed to fostering an inclusive workplace where diversity is valued, individuals are respected, and all qualified candidates are encouraged to apply.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why join Newmont
At Newmont, you'll be part of a global mining leader committed to safety, sustainability, and developing our people. We offer the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals, make a meaningful impact on workforce capability, and contribute to a culture where continuous learning, collaboration, and improvement are valued. Join a team that invests in your growth while helping shape the future of safe and productive mining operations.
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 43510 before the advertised closing date: 4 August 2026.

This position is part of a team responsible for the implementation and maintenance of the mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and exploration sites in Kainantu.  In addition, this position will also play and important role in the training of trades assistants.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.

Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.

“Join our team to drive high impact economic research and policy dialogue in partnership with government, academia, and development leaders in Papua New Guinea”
*Abt is committed to advancing women’s leadership in PNG’s economic development and are building an environment where women can lead progress and shape economic outcomes. Abt promotes an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment for women
This position includes a housing allowance, health insurance, and supportive workplace for parents and carers, including relevant leave and other benefits.
Port Moresby is a family post offering a vibrant mix of cultures, scenic coastal views, and welcoming local and international communities. Residents enjoy access to modern amenities including quality restaurants, supermarkets, hotels, and wildlife park, as well as outdoor activities including hiking, sailing, fishing and more.
About the Program
The
Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP)
is a flagship partnership supporting Papua New Guinea’s economic development priorities. Delivered by the Government of Australia in close collaboration with the Government of Papua New Guinea, APEP focuses on strengthening economic systems, institutions, and opportunities that support sustainable and inclusive growth through to 2028.
Working alongside government, research institutions, and development partners, APEP delivers coordinated and high‑impact outcomes across four key engagement areas:
Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods
Catalysing Economic Research and Dialogue
Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.
About the Opportunity
The Senior Program Manager (SPM), Economic Research & Dialogue (ERD) will work closely with APEP teams and externally with PNG partners and research institutions to shape and deliver high‑quality, policy‑relevant research that supports Papua New Guinea’s economic development.
The position will manage the design and implementation of research activities aligned to priority area of economic and social development including macro-economic policy, strengthening a business enabling environment, and agricultural growth in PNG.
Externally, the position will lead the management of key partnerships with Australia National University and the University of Papua New Guinea, as well as with other Australian academic institutions. Operations Manager – Rental Equipment
Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Ready to Lead the Next Phase of Growth?
High Arctic Energy Services is growing, evolving and investing in the future—and we're looking for a driven operational leader to be part of it.
With a strong reputation throughout Papua New Guinea and a growing footprint across the industrial, energy, mining and construction sectors, High Arctic is experiencing significant momentum. Our appointment as an Authorised Atlas Copco Distributor, continued fleet investment and expansion of the Rentals division have positioned the business for its next phase of growth.
Reporting directly to the General Manager – Rental Equipment, you will lead safe and efficient rental contract execution across mobilisation, operational delivery, maintenance coordination, fleet readiness, compliance and demobilisation.
This is a residential Port Moresby-based role operating on a family-friendly Monday to Friday roster, making it an attractive opportunity for professionals seeking long-term career growth and lifestyle stability in PNG.  PNG Nationals and current in-country expatriates are strongly encouraged to apply.
You'll be joining a leadership team that is passionate about growth, innovation, safety, developing national capability and delivering exceptional outcomes for customers throughout Papua New Guinea.
For the right person, this is more than a job—it's an opportunity to build something, leave a legacy and carve out a long-term leadership career with one of PNG's most recognised industrial services businesses.
Key Responsibilities
Lead safe and efficient end-to-end rental contract execution from mobilisation through operational delivery, maintenance coordination and demobilisation.
Ensure fleet reliability, utilisation, compliance and readiness across cranes, generators, compressors, pumps, telehandlers, EWPs, camps and heavy support equipment.
Coordinate logistics, maintenance activities, inspections and operational resources.
Act as the primary operational contact for customers during active hires, ensuring clear communication, rapid issue resolution and high service standards throughout the contract lifecycle.
Build and maintain strong relationships with customers, contractors and internal stakeholders.
Lead, mentor and develop operational teams, with a strong focus on developing national employees, succession capability, safety, accountability and continuous improvement.
Drive operational excellence through planning, cost control, equipment performance and process improvement.
Support business growth through customer engagement, operational expertise and strategic fleet planning.
Support business growth by understanding the rental sales process, identifying customer opportunities during active hires, and working with the Sales Manager to develop leads into practical rental solutions.
Why You'll Love This Opportunity
This is a rare opportunity to join a growing and well-established PNG business at an exciting point in its evolution.  We Offer:
Generous remuneration package
Company-provided vehicle
Family-friendly Monday to Friday roster
Senior leadership role with autonomy and influence
Exposure to major mining, energy, construction and industrial projects
Genuine opportunity to shape a growing business unit
Long-term career development and progression opportunities
If you're looking for a role where you can make a genuine impact while enjoying an attractive expatriate-style package and lifestyle-friendly roster, this is an opportunity not to be missed.
About You
You are an experienced operational leader with a strong background in heavy equipment rentals, mining, construction, oil & gas, logistics or industrial services.
Essential
Proven experience leading operational teams and managing complex mobilisation, logistics and field operations.
Strong technical understanding of cranes, generators, compressors, pumps, telehandlers, EWPs, camp assets and heavy support equipment.
Strong leadership, communication and stakeholder management skills.
Commercially minded with the ability to balance customer outcomes, operational performance and cost control.
Commercially aware, with an understanding of the rental sales process and the ability to identify customer needs, leads and growth opportunities through day-to-day operational engagement.
Commitment to safety, compliance and continuous improvement.
Current driver's licence and ability to travel throughout PNG as required.
Highly Regarded
Understanding of PNG business practices, stakeholder management and cultural environments.
Trade, technical, engineering or operational qualifications.
Experience using maintenance or asset management systems (CMMS).
Candidates with demonstrated PNG experience and established professional networks within PNG will be highly regarded.
Apply Now

27822.description:
Operational
Performance Coach
PNG Expat Opportunity | 28/28 Rotation | PNG Based role
Ready to take your drilling career beyond day-to-day operations into performance leadership?
High Arctic Energy Services is seeking an experienced
Operational Performance Coach
to support drilling operations across our sites in Papua New Guinea.
High Arctic has built a strong reputation in Papua New Guinea through its commitment to operational excellence, employee development and community engagement. We combine the capability of a leading drilling contractor with the agility of a smaller organisation, creating opportunities for our people to grow, influence outcomes and build rewarding careers.
This is a unique opportunity for an accomplished drilling professional who enjoys improving operational performance, coaching teams, challenging assumptions and helping organisations learn from experience.
Working alongside experienced drilling supervisors, rig leadership teams, engineers and contractors, you'll provide an independent performance lens that helps ensure plans are executed effectively, lessons are captured and operational performance continues to improve. This role is focused on operational excellence, disciplined execution and creating a culture of continuous improvement across our drilling operations.
About the Role
This is
not a traditional drilling supervision role.
Our rigs are staffed by experienced drilling professionals. Reporting to the Chief Operations Offficer, your role is to provide an independent performance perspective, helping operational teams understand what is working, what isn't, and where opportunities exist to improve execution and performance.   Key responsibilities include:
Monitoring operational performance against approved plans and schedules.
Identifying execution gaps, operational inefficiencies and non-productive time (NPT).
Facilitating operational reviews, after-action reviews and lessons learned sessions.
Supporting operational readiness and planning reviews.
Developing performance reporting and KPI dashboards.
Promoting operational discipline and adherence to agreed work processes.
Driving accountability for operational commitments and improvement actions.
Assisting teams to identify root causes and implement sustainable solutions.
Leading knowledge capture and continuous improvement initiatives.
Supporting a strong safety and operational excellence culture across drilling operations.
Our ideal candidate
You’re a respected extractive industry professional who gains satisfaction from helping teams improve performance, not just delivering operations.
You have the credibility to engage experienced crews and leaders, the curiosity to understand why results vary from plan, and the confidence to challenge constructively when improvement opportunities exist.
You build trust, ask the right questions and help teams translate lessons learned into better execution. You're motivated by accountability, operational discipline and continuous improvement, and you take pride in helping people and operations perform at their best.
You'll bring substantial experience in drilling, wellsite operations or other high-risk environments, along with strong coaching, communication and influencing skills.
You will possess a minimum Diploma Level qualification in; Health & Safety, Frontline Management, Leadership, Coaching or similar disciplines
What Success Looks Like
Success in this role isn't measured by the number of wells drilled, success is measured by:
Improved adherence to operational plans.
Reduced execution variances.
Improved operational readiness.
Stronger accountability across crews and contractors.
Effective closure of lessons learned and improvement actions.
Reduced recurring performance losses.
Enhanced knowledge sharing across operations.
Better operational outcomes through disciplined execution.
Why Join Us?
This is a rare opportunity to influence the performance of a major drilling operation without being responsible for day-to-day drilling supervision.
You will work directly with highly experienced operational teams, helping to improve consistency, execution quality, operational learning and overall performance.
If you're the type of person who notices when reality differs from the plan, asks why, and helps teams perform better the next time, we'd like to hear from you.  You'll also enjoy:
28/28 roster
Company-funded flights
Quality accommodation and camp facilities
Excellent food and site amenities
Exposure to world-class drilling operations supporting our client
A strong team culture built on respect, safety and performance
Career growth opportunities within a smaller, agile organisation where your contribution is visible and valued
The opportunity to help shape how drilling operations are executed, reviewed and continuously improved
If you're looking for a role where your drilling experience can directly influence operational performance, develop capability within teams and help shape the future of drilling operations, we'd love to hear from you.
Apply Now
Become part of a team committed to operational excellence, continuous improvement and world-class drilling performance.
If your experience, skills, qualifications, and attributes meet the above-nominated specifications, please email your CV, Qualifications, References, and Licenses to:
[email protected]

The company holds a premier portfolio of assets in PNG, including the historical Tolukuma Gold Mine located 100km north of Port Moresby in the Goilala District, Central Province, alongside extensive exploration holdings in Central and New Britain Provinces.

Develop and maintain operational procedures, metallurgical accounting systems, and quality control processes.

Prepare daily reports on safety issues, production figures, and metallurgical test results.

27866.description:
Experienced Panel Manager
(The quality-control, no-comebacks kind)
Important: If you do not have proven panel shop or collision repair management experience, please do not submit your CV.
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s leading automotive groups, representing brands like Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Our workshops and repair operations depend on accuracy, discipline, quality workmanship, and strong leadership.
We’re looking for an experienced Panel Manager to lead panel repair operations and make sure every job is managed properly from assessment through to completion.
This is not a role for someone who only understands the theory. We need someone who knows panel repairs, understands workshop flow, can manage tradesmen, and can keep quality, timelines, and customer expectations under control.
If your experience is limited, this is not the one to test it on.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for managing the day-to-day operations of the panel shop, including job allocation, repair planning, workflow, quality control, staff supervision, and customer/job updates.
That includes assessing repair requirements, coordinating panel beating and paint work, checking job cards, monitoring repair progress, managing parts requirements, and making sure vehicles are repaired to a high standard before delivery.
You’ll work closely with service advisors, parts teams, technicians, insurers, customers, and management to make sure each job is handled professionally and completed on time.
You’ll also be responsible for maintaining workshop discipline, safe work practices, productivity, and proper reporting.
The expectation is simple: manage the job properly, control the quality, deliver the vehicle properly.
Who This Suits
This role suits an experienced Panel Manager or senior panel repair professional with real workshop leadership experience.
You understand panel beating, collision repair, paint preparation, refinishing standards, repair estimates, job costing, parts coordination, and workshop scheduling.
You know how to manage people, not just jobs. You can lead tradesmen, control workflow, deal with pressure, and make sure standards do not drop when the workshop gets busy.
You should be confident checking repair quality, identifying poor workmanship, solving bottlenecks, and making sure vehicles do not leave the shop with avoidable defects.
You keep your paperwork accurate, your team accountable, and your standards high.
If people already rely on you to bring order to a busy panel shop, this will feel familiar.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors operates a busy automotive business with real volume, recognised global brands, and high customer expectations.
You’ll be working with experienced teams who understand that good panel work is not just about fixing damage — it is about safety, appearance, customer confidence, and protecting the reputation of the business.
This is a role where leadership matters, quality is noticed, and strong workshop managers are taken seriously.
