27862.description:
About Newmont
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation is located on Aniolam Island in Papua New Guinea’s New Ireland Province. Lihir is one of the world’s largest producing gold operations and is situated within a geothermally active, extinct volcanic crater near the town of Londolovit. As a major open-pit gold operation, Lihir plays an important role in Newmont’s global portfolio and contributes significant economic and social value to Papua New Guinea and local communities.
Your role
As the Superintendent, Power & Utilities Operations, you will lead Power and Utilities operations across the Lihir operation, with a strong focus on safe, reliable and efficient power generation.
This role is responsible for monitoring, diagnosing and improving power generation operations on Lihir Island in line with site standards and country regulations. You will oversee power and utilities assets, guide operational performance, manage risk, develop teams and support continuous improvement across a 24-hour operating environment.
This is a key residential leadership role for an experienced power station or power generation professional who has led teams, managed operational performance and understands the systems, networks and controls required to run safe and reliable power generation operations.
Key Responsibilities
Oversee Power and Utilities operations across department assets, ensuring safe, reliable and efficient performance.
Develop operational procedures and guidelines to support effective operation of power assets.
Monitor, diagnose and improve team performance, implementing improvement strategies where required.
Monitor asset and team performance metrics, including KPIs, reliability measures and operational trends.
Complete operational and statutory reporting in line with site and regulatory requirements.
Develop budgets, resource plans and operational requirements for power and utilities activities.
Conduct regular inspections and safety audits across power and utilities systems.
Identify and resolve operational issues, streamlining power and utilities processes where possible.
Coach and guide power and utilities team members on procedures, safety expectations and operational requirements.
Identify operational risks, implement mitigation measures and continuously monitor risk controls.
Your Skills & Experience
Demonstrated experience in power station, power generation or power utilities operations.
Strong understanding of power plant systems, power generation operations and associated networks.
Previous leadership experience, ideally in a superintendent, supervisor, team leader or power station management role.
Experience leading, coaching and developing operational teams in a 24-hour operating environment.
Ability to monitor, diagnose and improve operational and team performance.
Strong understanding of safety compliance, risk management and environmental requirements within power or utilities operations.
Experience with operational scheduling, performance monitoring, reporting and continuous improvement.
Budgeting, resource planning and cost management experience.
Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to interact, influence and resolve issues across operations, maintenance, technical teams, contractors and service providers.
Ability and willingness to work residentially on Lihir Island on a 5 days on / 2 days off roster.
Desirable experience includes a bachelor’s degree in Engineering, a trade certificate, power station operator certification, or equivalent practical power generation leadership experience. Mining experience is not essential; candidates from power generation, utilities, PNG Power, industrial operations, oil and gas, manufacturing or other relevant power plant environments are encouraged to apply where they bring strong power station operations and people leadership experience.
Work Environment & Benefits
This is a full-time residential PNG national role based at Lihir Gold Limited in Papua New Guinea, working on a 5 days on / 2 days off roster. You will support Operations and Process Operations, leading a Power and Utilities team that supports critical site infrastructure and 24-hour operational requirements.
You will work closely with cross-functional superintendents, supervisors, advisors, specialists, project teams, health and safety, environmental teams, technicians, engineers, regulatory bodies, government stakeholders, suppliers and service providers.
This role offers the opportunity to step into a key site leadership position where your power generation experience will directly support safe, reliable and sustainable operations at one of Newmont’s major PNG operations.
Why join Newmont?
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.
Learn more about our purpose and values: About Newmont
Hear from our people: Life at Newmont
Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team:
[email protected]
.
Apply

27821.description:
PNG's First 100% Nationally Owned Producer
Driving Sustainable & Affordable Energy Growth
Securing Energy Future Through Local Ownership
The opportunity
Our client is a key player in the renewable energy and power generation sector in Papua New Guinea. They are dedicated to developing critical infrastructure and navigating the country's intricate regulatory framework to provide sustainable energy solutions. By joining this high-performing team, you will contribute to the strategic legal oversight that empowers large-scale energy projects and ensures operational excellence across the organization.
The role
The Project Engineer role is pivotal to this mission. You will drive the company's continued success by assisting in the planning, development, and engineering design of solar, mini-grid, and electrical distribution projects. This includes reviewing engineering designs, conducting detailed site assessments, preparing technical specifications, and ensuring full compliance with local and international electrical regulations. This role requires extensive collaboration with cross-functional teams—including Engineering, Finance, Procurement, and external contractors—to align technical execution with overall project objectives.
This is a perfect opportunity if you are a positive, professional, and reliable engineering specialist with a strong background in power and renewable energy systems. You will leverage your technical expertise in a fast-paced environment to manage project parameters, perform quality assurance, and secure the operational integrity of critical energy infrastructure.
Main duties include:
Support Engineering Design: Assist the engineering team in design and contractor management for rooftop solar and mini-grid installations, utilizing specialized industry design software.
Conduct Site Assessments: Lead scoping, data collection, and energy sizing analysis for potential mini-grid and solar sites across Papua New Guinea.
Draft Technical Documentation: Formulate project parameters, specifications, and scopes of work, while assisting in the preparation of pre-feasibility studies, cost estimates, and RFQ/tender documents.
Ensure Quality & Compliance: Perform quality assurance and control tasks on contractor budgets, schedules, and performance to ensure compliance with relevant electrical regulations, applicable codes, and company policies.
Monitor Project Metrics: Create frameworks to monitor and measure project data, and establish performance test methods to verify the quality of completed installations.
Collaborate & Engage: Work closely with internal stakeholders, local communities, regulatory bodies, and contractors to facilitate smooth project delivery and execution.
Qualification and Experience:
Bachelor's degree in Engineering or a closely related field.
Current registration with the Institution of Engineers Papua New Guinea (IEPNG) and possesses a valid driver's license.
5+ years of proven experience within the power and renewables (or closely related) industry.
Hands-on experience with electrical or renewable design software such as Helioscope, AutoCAD, or PowerWorld, alongside a strong knowledge of local and international electrical regulations.
Possesses advanced written and verbal communication skills, with a demonstrated ability to write technical reports, deliver impactful presentations, and manage stakeholders effectively.
An organized and proactive planner with excellent project management skills, capable of working collaboratively with cross-functional teams while managing tight deadlines.

27597.description:
Recruitment Officer
PCS: People & Culture Services - Port Moresby, NCD
Position Title: Recruitment Officer
Department: People & Culture
Location: IBSUniversity, 11 Mile Campus
Reports To: Recruitment Manager
Employment Type: Full-Time
Position Overview
The Recruitment Officer is responsible for managing and executing the end-to-end recruitment
process to attract, select, and onboard top talent for IBSUniversity. This role requires building strong
relationships with hiring managers, developing innovative sourcing strategies, and ensuring a positive
candidate experience to support the university's strategic goals. The officer also manages labor and
immigration processes for expatriates and their dependents.
Key Responsibilities
1. Recruitment Planning and Strategy
Collaborate with department heads to understand current and future workforce
requirements.
Develop job descriptions and specifications in consultation with hiring managers.
Create and implement recruitment plans to attract a diverse pool of qualified
candidates.
Stay updated on market trends to adjust strategies for hard-to-fill or critical roles.
2. Sourcing and Advertising
Develop and execute creative sourcing strategies to identify potential candidates
through online job boards, social media platforms, recruitment agencies, and
employee referrals.
Design and post engaging job advertisements to attract quality candidates.
Build and maintain a talent pipeline for current and future hiring needs.
3. Screening and Selection
Review applications and shortlist candidates based on qualifications, experience, and
role requirements.
Conduct initial phone screenings to assess candidate suitability.
Schedule, coordinate, and participate in interviews with hiring managers and panel
members.
Administer pre-employment assessments and conduct reference and background
checks.
4. Offer Management and Onboarding
Prepare and negotiate employment offers in alignment with organizational policies.
Coordinate the onboarding process for new hires, ensuring all documentation and
orientation requirements are met.
Liaise with payroll and other departments to ensure a seamless transition for new
employees.
5. Candidate Experience
Ensure timely communication with candidates throughout the recruitment process.
Provide constructive feedback to unsuccessful candidates when requested.
Promote IBS University as an employer of choice by delivering a positive candidate
experience.
6. Reporting and Metrics
Maintain accurate and up-to-date recruitment records.
Generate reports on recruitment metrics, including time-to-hire, cost-per-hire, and
candidate satisfaction.
Evaluate the effectiveness of recruitment efforts and recommend improvements.
7. Compliance
Ensure recruitment practices comply with employment laws and university policies.
Maintain confidentiality of sensitive candidate and organizational information.
8. Labor and Immigration Processes
Manage expatriate recruitment, including coordination of work permits and visas for
new hires, their dependents, and existing expatriate staff and their dependents.
Handle renewals of work permits and visas for expatriate staff and dependents in a
timely manner.
Fast-track work permits and visas through networks and other creative solutions to
minimize delays.
Liaise with government authorities and agencies to ensure compliance with labor
and immigration regulations.
Key Qualifications and Skills
Education/Qualification
Bachelor’s degree/Diploma in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field.
Experience
Proven experience in end-to-end recruitment, preferably in higher education or a similar
industry.
Familiarity with labor and immigration processes for expatriates and their dependents is an
advantage.
Skills and Competencies
Strong understanding of recruitment and selection processes.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Proficiency in sourcing candidates through various channels.
Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to handle multiple
priorities.
Attention to detail and problem-solving ability.
Ability to build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)
Time-to-hire for each position.
Cost-per-hire relative to budget.
Quality of hires based on performance and retention metrics.
Candidate satisfaction scores from surveys or feedback.
Recruitment process adherence to policies and timelines.
Timely and efficient processing of work permits and visas.
Working Conditions
Full-time role based at IBSUniversity, with occasional travel for recruitment fairs and events.
Ability to work extended hours during peak recruitment periods.
Apply

Lead client acquisition and deepen key SME relationships.

Expatriate Opportunity
A growing SME banking business within an established bank in Papua New Guinea is looking for a Head of Business Banking to set the strategic direction and personally drive new business growth.
This isn’t a role for someone who wants to oversee from a distance — the SME team is expanding, and you’ll need to be hands-on, leading from the front on both strategy and business development. Set out and establish the strategic framework for the SME banking business

27497.description:
Summary
The selected candidate will oversee all accounting operations, including accounts payable, receivable, and financial reporting. This role involves managing a team of accountants to ensure accurate recording of financial transactions, compliance with tax regulations, and preparation of audit materials. S/he will specifically focus on accounting functions and collaborate with the Finance Department on related financial planning and analysis activities.
Duties and Responsibilities
1) Accounting Operations (AP, AR, GL)
Oversee accounts payable and receivable processes to ensure timely and accurate processing of payments, receipts, and allocations.
Ensure customer and vendor reconciliations are performed and reviewed, including monitoring of aging reports and follow-up actions.
Maintain accurate general ledger postings and ensure proper supporting documentation for all transactions.
Manage month-end close activities, including review of journals, accruals, prepayments, and account reconciliations.
2) Retail Accounting and POS Control
Ensure monthly billing and retail sales reporting is complete and accurate.
Reconcile point-of-sale (POS) data to accounting records and investigate variances with Retail Operations.
Monitor inventory accounting movements and support inventory turnover reporting and reconciliation.
3) Financial Reporting (Preparation and Accuracy)
Prepare monthly, quarterly, and annual financial statements in line with IFRS/GAAP and company policies.
Prepare monthly management reports, including P&L statements and key supporting schedules for review by the CFO/Financial Controller.
Ensure financial reports are complete, accurate, and supported by reconciliation schedules before submission for internal review.
4) Operational Financial Controls (Monitor and Escalate)
Implement and enforce accounting policies and procedures to safeguard assets and maintain financial integrity.
Ensure segregation of duties is applied within AP, AR, cash handling, POS processes, and journal approvals.
Review high-risk areas and exception items, including manual journal entries, credit notes, write-offs, adjustments, refunds, and unusual vendor/customer activity.
Perform variance and exception reviews (e.g., unusual movements, out-of-pattern transactions, repeated overrides) and document findings.
Escalate suspicious transactions, control breaches, or significant variances to the CFO/Financial Controller and support follow-up actions.
Support Internal Audit by providing documents, explanations, and evidence of control performance (without compromising audit independence).
5) Tax and Statutory Compliance
Ensure compliance with tax regulations, including preparation and filing of corporate tax returns, VAT/GST, and payroll-related taxes where applicable.
Maintain accurate tax working papers and coordinate with tax consultants and authorities as required.
Ensure adherence to applicable IAS and local regulatory requirements.
6) Audit Coordination and Close-Out
Serve as the main contact for external auditors for accounting matters.
Prepare audit schedules and provide supporting documents and explanations in a timely manner.
Track audit findings and implement agreed corrective actions within Finance to strengthen controls and improve compliance.
7) Systems, Process Improvement, and Data Integrity
Ensure accounting systems and processes are optimised for accuracy, efficiency, and proper access control.
Work with IT and relevant departments to improve integration between ERP/accounting systems and other platforms (including POS).
Maintain proper master data controls (customers, vendors, chart of accounts) and data integrity within systems.
8) Team Leadership and Capability Building
Lead and develop the accounting team to ensure effective delivery of daily operations and month-end close.
Assign responsibilities, monitor performance, and ensure staff follow SOPs and control procedures.
Conduct performance reviews and provide coaching and training to improve skills and compliance.
Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, and professionalism within the department.
Job Requirements
CPA or ACCA or equivalent professional accounting certification (required).
Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field (required).
Minimum 10 years of accounting experience, with at least 2 years in a supervisory or management role.
Proven experience managing AP, AR, general ledger, and month-end close.
Experience supporting retail accounting operations, including POS reconciliations and P&L reporting.
Experience supporting audits and implementing corrective actions from findings.
Strong knowledge of IFRS/GAAP, tax regulations, and audit requirements.
Proficiency with accounting software and ERP systems; familiarity with retail POS systems.
Strong skills in reconciliations, reporting, and operational control monitoring.
High attention to detail and strong quality control habits.
Strong leadership and team management capability.
Strong analytical skills with ability to identify exceptions and control issues.
Clear communication skills and ability to escalate issues with evidence and recommendations.
Strong organisation and ability to manage deadlines and multiple priorities.

" in the email's subject to ensure your application is processed.

More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Fixed Plant Maintenance team, the Senior Maintenance Planner ensures that all routine maintenance activities for our process plant are appropriately planned (with input from operations and maintenance) so that the work can progress in a safe, environmentally responsible, efficient, cost effective and repeatable manner.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Actively promote a safe and healthy culture. Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions. Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Develop and implement maintenance schedules for both planned and corrective maintenance activities to ensure equipment reliability and operational efficiency in multiple areas
Utilise Pronto to track Planned jobs (Weekly and Shutdowns), work orders, manage maintenance backlogs, and ensure timely completion of tasks.
Assists in the development of Maintenance budgets and reporting actual performance against budgets and plans.
Track and forecast critical component requirements to prevent unscheduled downtime, while monitoring component life cycles and managing replacements in alignment with predictive maintenance strategies.
Develop and track key performance indicators (KPIs) to analyse equipment performance and reliability. Implement corrective actions to enhance equipment reliability and reduce unplanned breakdowns including but not limited to:
Coordinate with procurement team to ensure timely acquisition of parts and components while maintaining optimal stock levels to minimise excess inventory costs. Conduct regular inventory reviews, request stock adjustments, and ensure accurate inventory records within Pronto, updating them as required based on usage trends.
Coordinate with procurement and logistics teams to secure the availability of spare parts and components, reducing delays in maintenance activities.
Prepare structured reports to provide insights into maintenance performance, downtime trends, and cost analysis. Maintain accurate maintenance records and generate data-driven insights for continuous improvement. Check quality of daily, weekly, and monthly KPI reports while also preparing and maintaining quarterly, 6monthly, and annual maintenance forecasts.
Additionally, assist and develop the national workforce in maintenance planning, scheduling, and execution processes, fostering skill development and knowledge transfer.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have mechanical or electrical trade qualifications as well as a technical qualification in Maintenance Planning. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Five (5) years’ experience in computer-based maintenance planning/scheduling.
Must have experience in using Pronto ERP
Must have advanced skills in MS Excel and MS Projects.
Strong understanding of Reliability Centered Maintenance.

Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

This position is part of a team responsible for the implementation and maintenance of the mine power supply and distribution system for all electrical equipment on the mine and exploration sites in Kainantu. Key / Major Accountabilities

Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.

Experience in installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control Centre’s, LV and HV transfers and starters.

Ability to train maintenance personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is high.
Good health physical ability is a prerequisite, as is the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.

Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. CLIMATE CHANGE CHILD PROTECTION OFFICER
(POM BASED)
ChildFund PNG is seeking a dedicated and experienced
Child Protection Officer
to promote and safeguard the rights and wellbeing of children within our programmes and activities. The role is responsible for implementing child protection policies, responding to child safeguarding concerns, conducting risk assessments, providing training and awareness sessions, and coordinating with communities, government agencies, and other stakeholders to ensure children are protected from abuse, neglect, exploitation, and violence. The successful candidate will monitor compliance with safeguarding standards, maintain accurate case documentation, and support the development of a safe and child-friendly environment for all children.
Key qualities:
Strong understanding of child protection principles, excellent communication and case management skills, high ethical standards, and a commitment to child rights and safeguarding practices.
ESSENTIAL QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE
Bachelor’s degree in social work, Community Development, Child Protection, Development Studies, Psychology, Sociology, Education, Humanitarian Studies or another relevant field.
Minimum three years of relevant experience in child protection, GBV, safeguarding, community development, humanitarian programming, climate resilience, education, social services or related work.
Experience working directly with communities, children, adolescents, parents, volunteers and local leaders.
Experience supporting project planning, field implementation, training, monitoring, documentation and reporting.
Experience working with government agencies, schools, civil society organisations or development partners is highly desirable.
Practical knowledge of child protection referral pathways, safeguarding, PSEA, confidentiality and survivor-centred approaches.
Knowledge of CPiE, psychological first aid, Child-Friendly Spaces, case management or climate/DRR programming is an advantage.
Previous experience in Central Province or rural and remote PNG communities is an advantage.
CHILD SAFEGUARDING REQUIREMENTS
This position involves regular direct contact with children, adolescents, families and vulnerable people. Appointment will be subject to ChildFund PNG’s recruitment checks, and the successful candidate must sign and comply with the Child Safeguarding Policy, Code of Conduct, PSEA requirements and all related safeguarding procedures. Any offer of employment may be withdrawn or employment terminated where safeguarding requirements are not met.

27810.description:
Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference.
About Lihir
Lihir is one of the world's largest gold mining operations, located on Niolam Island in Papua New Guinea's New Ireland Province. The operation is renowned for its unique volcanic landscape and combines world-class mining and processing with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability,  innovation and technical excellence.
The operation combines open-pit mining and gold processing in a remote island setting, supported by modern facilities and a culture focused on improving daily.
At Lihir, you'll be part of a team that is deeply connected to the island and the communities that call it home. We are committed to creating lasting benefits through local employment, training, scholarships and apprenticeship programs, while fostering a workplace where people look out for one another and succeed together.
With a culture grounded in safety, respect and delivering responsibly, Lihir offers the opportunity to develop your career while contributing to an operation that plays an important role in Papua New Guinea's economic and social development.
Your Impact
As an Advisor – People Training (Drilling), you will play a critical role in developing the capability, safety and performance of our drilling workforce. Through coaching, mentoring, assessment and training delivery, you will ensure our people have the skills, confidence and knowledge required to operate safely and effectively. Your contribution will directly support operational excellence, workforce development and safe production outcomes.
As part of our team, you will
Develop, deliver and continuously improve training programs, assessment tools and learning materials for drilling operations, specifically facilitate operator training on PV231 and D65 drill training.
Facilitate both classroom-based and practical on-the-job training across drilling equipment, procedures and associated operational activities.
Conduct competency assessments, provide coaching and mentoring, and support employees throughout their development journey.
Conduct field observations and engage with Supervisors and Superintendents to identify capability gaps and training needs.
Partner with operational leaders to tailor training solutions that support business objectives and workforce capability requirements.
Ensure all training programs align with company, industry and HSE standards.
Maintain accurate competency and training records within the Learning Management System (LMS).
Promote proactive safety behaviours and a culture of continuous improvement.
Coordinate and manage training resources, including PPE, equipment and training materials.
Foster an inclusive environment where collaboration, feedback and continuous learning are encouraged.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this position, you will bring:
Minimum 5 years' experience in Open Pit Mining Operations as a Driller, Supervisor, Trainer or similar role.
Certificate III in Training and Assessment (or equivalent qualification in education or training).
Demonstrated expertise in training within the mining industry.
Experience developing training materials, assessments and learning programs.
Strong understanding of adult learning principles, facilitation techniques and vocational education and training (VET) processes.
Experience delivering both practical field-based and classroom training.
Proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint, together with experience using Learning Management Systems.
Excellent communication, coaching and stakeholder engagement skills.
Ability to build strong working relationships across operational and support teams.
Strong commitment to safety, continuous improvement and workforce development.
Operator training qualifications (eg. Epiroc).
PNG Driver Licence Class 6 and 7 (or ability to obtain).
Your work environment
You'll join a collaborative and values-driven team focused on building workforce capability and supporting safe, productive mining operations. Working closely with Mine Operations, Health & Safety, Human Resources, Supervisors and Superintendents, you'll have the opportunity to influence learning outcomes across the business while helping create an inclusive culture where people can learn, grow and perform at their best.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why join Newmont
At Newmont, you'll be part of a global mining leader committed to safety, sustainability, and developing our people. We offer the opportunity to work alongside experienced professionals, make a meaningful impact on workforce capability, and contribute to a culture where continuous learning, collaboration, and improvement are valued. Join a team that invests in your growth while helping shape the future of safe and productive mining operations.
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 43826 before the advertised closing date: 30 July 2026.
At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining.​

26614.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position is responsible for the service and maintenance of fixed plant equipment in a safe and appropriate manner. You will ensure a preventative maintenance schedule is adhered to as well as perform reactive maintenance when equipment breaks down to ensure downtime of machinery is minimized.
Key Accountabilities
Maintain and repair fixed plant equipment onsite in a safe, responsible and timely and effective manner ensuring all Fixed Plant and K92 mining standards are met.
Oversee installation, operation, repairs, and maintenance of the Fixed Plant equipment and infrastructures.
Maintain all plant equipment and ensure all planning and scheduling maintenance activities are performed safely and more effectively.
Assist the Maintenance Foreman in performing preventative maintenance programs, perform routine maintenance and enforces statutory requirements and assist to create a zero-base safety culture.
Ensure safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
The successful completion of daily work to meet quality standards and deadlines.
Reporting faults and hazards and respond to routine emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area.
Monitoring and assessment of plant and equipment.
Exercise due care and attention to work in a safe and efficient manner.
Assist in supervising and on-job training for Apprentices and Trade Assistance.
Willingness to assist other trades as and when required.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will have certificates from a recognized Tertiary institution or technical training program in a maintenance trade or completion of a recognized apprenticeship program, or combination of the two.
Trade Certificate Fitting & Machinery / Mechanical Fitting.
Sound knowledge of all Processing Plant Equipment or similar.
Possess the ability to troubleshoot and perform root cause analysis (particularly in diagnosis and fault finding).
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the equipment availability is maintained and the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Good working knowledge of the principles and practices of OH&S and Fixed Plant.
Be flexible and adaptable to the needs of the business and ability to work harmoniously as part of the team.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP
Apply

27793.description:
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritising the wellbeing of our employees, the environment and the local communities.
Our commitment to safety, innovation and responsible mining ensures we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions in which we operate. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact by fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual as a
Security Screening Supervisor.
About the role
Reporting to the Chief Duty Officer, the Security Screening Supervisor is responsible for leading security screening, personnel searching, access control and guard force operations at designated security screening facilities and critical entry control points across the Porgera Mine.
The position plays a key role within the Asset Protection Department by providing professional supervision of guard force personnel while ensuring all employees, contractors and visitors entering or leaving controlled areas are processed safely, efficiently and in accordance with New Porgera Limited's security standards.
Guard Force Protection Officers are responsible for maintaining the integrity of the mine's access control system through the effective application of searching, screening and inspection procedures using modern security technologies, including body scanners, baggage scanners, walk-through metal detectors and other security screening equipment.
The role requires exceptional professionalism, integrity, leadership, attention to detail and sound judgement. Successful applicants must demonstrate the ability to supervise local guard force personnel, make independent decisions and maintain high standards of customer service while enforcing security requirements in a busy operational environment.
In this role, you will:
Supervise Guard Force personnel deployed at security screening facilities and access control points.
Lead daily searching and screening operations using approved security technologies and procedures.
Conduct personnel, baggage, vehicle and property searches in accordance with APD Standard Operating Procedures.
Operate body scanners, baggage scanners, walk-through metal detectors and associated screening equipment.
Ensure all persons entering and exiting controlled areas comply with access control requirements.
Detect and prevent the unauthorised removal of Gold Bearing Material (GBM), company property, prohibited items and other security risks.
Maintain the integrity of access control systems through accurate identification, verification and visitor management procedures.
Monitor compliance with company security policies and respond appropriately to security incidents.
Coach, mentor and lead Guard Force personnel to maintain professional standards and continuous improvement.
Complete incident reports, search records and operational documentation accurately and in a timely manner.
Promote a positive customer service culture while maintaining the highest standards of security.
Maintain a strong commitment to workplace safety and compliance with all APD procedures.
What we are looking for
We are seeking highly professional security personnel who demonstrate integrity, leadership, initiative and a strong commitment to protecting people, assets and operations.
Successful applicants will possess excellent communication skills, a high level of personal presentation, strong observational abilities and the confidence to make sound decisions while working in a dynamic operational environment.
Experience in security screening, aviation security, corrections, law enforcement, military, mining security or critical infrastructure security will be highly regarded.
Previous experience supervising security screening operations and guard force personnel will be considered an advantage.
Experience as a Security Dog (K9) Handler is desirable but not essential.
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Grade 10 qualification as a minimum.
Minimum three years' experience in security, law enforcement, military or mining security.
Previous experience supervising or leading security personnel.
Demonstrated experience in access control, personnel searching or security screening.
Strong leadership and people management skills.
High attention to detail and ability to identify suspicious behaviour.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.
Ability to remain calm and make sound decisions under pressure.
High level of integrity, professionalism and personal accountability.
Ability to learn and operate modern electronic security screening systems.
Current Security Industry qualifications will be highly regarded.
Previous Security Dog (K9) handling experience will be highly regarded but is not essential
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a
Security Screening Supervisor
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a
Security Screening Supervisor
. This role offers a unique opportunity to work in a dynamic team, work with cutting edge security technology in a mining environment and contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your leadership and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.

27787.description:
Company :
Hastings Deering (PNG) Limited
About Us:
Hastings Deering (PNG) Ltd is one of the largest Caterpillar dealer networks in the world. We sell, service and support the complete range of Caterpillar machinery used in the mining, construction, agricultural, materials handling and government sectors.  Over the last 75 years, we have built a reputation for hiring and developing the industry’s best and delivering an exemplary level of service to our customers and colleagues.
About the Role:
We currently have an excellent opportunity for a
Continuous Improvement Project Officer
to join our Continuous Improvement team based in Port Moresby. This role primarily exists for coordinating and delivering business improvement projects that enhance operational effectiveness, process efficiency, governance, and customer outcomes across the organisation. The role leads and supports process management initiatives, gap analysis, policy and procedure development, standard work implementation, and continuous improvement projects using Lean, CPS, and process improvement methodologies to drive sustainable business performance improvements.
Reporting to the
Country General Manager, PNG & SI
, the Continuous Improvement Project Officer will be responsible for:
Ensure safety goals are achieved through personal commitment, no harm to self or others and participation in safety initiatives.
Display fairness, exhibit trust and create real teamwork and sharing.
Proactively seek and maintain collaborative working relationships with peers and managers to deliver results.
Ensure opportunities for continuous improvement are identified and reported
Develop, review, implement, and maintain business policies, procedures, standard operating procedures (SOPs), standard work, and governance documentation to ensure consistency, compliance, and operational excellence across the organisation.
Conduct business process reviews, process mapping, and gap analyses to identify inefficiencies, risks, compliance gaps, and opportunities for improving operational performance and customer outcomes.
Monitor and report on project performance, improvement initiatives, risks, actions, compliance requirements, and realized benefits, ensuring effective governance and timely escalation of issues where required.
Manage document control and process governance frameworks, ensuring business documentation remains accurate, current, accessible, and compliant with organizational standards.
Carry out CPS Green Belt project tasks as assigned by Management
Facilitate stakeholder engagement, workshops, training, and change management activities to support the successful adoption and sustainability of process improvements and business initiatives.
Apply Lean, CPS, Six Sigma, and continuous improvement methodologies to eliminate waste, improve process effectiveness, standardize work practices, and deliver measurable business benefits.
About You:
Education/Qualifications:
Project Management certification or equivalent knowledge.
CPS Lean Yellow Belt certification.
Lean Green Belt, CPS Green Belt, or equivalent Continuous Improvement certification.
Bachelor’s degree in business management, Administration, Operations Management, Organisational Development, or a related discipline.
Experience:
Minimum 3 years' experience in continuous improvement, business process management, project coordination, or business analysis.
Minimum 2 years' experience applying Green Belt methodologies.
Experience delivering improvement initiatives from planning through to sustainable implementation.
Strong stakeholder engagement and influencing skills.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft 365 applications.
Experience documenting business processes, SOPs, procedures, and policies.
Working knowledge of Lean, CPS, Six Sigma, Kaizen, or Operational Excellence methodologies.
Experience facilitating workshops, process mapping, and stakeholder consultations.
Experience in mining, heavy industry, logistics, construction, or service operations.
Proficiency in process mapping and workflow management tools.
“Only candidates based in Port Moresby are encouraged to apply”.
To express interest in this challenging and rewarding role, submit your application including current updated CV, copies of certificates, references, valid police clearance and apply via Workday Career page.
To Apply: Click on the “Apply”
button.
Enquiries: Please call our HR Team on (675) 300 8300
Only Shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
Applications close Wednesday 29th July 2026.
Apply
